title: Newton’s Second Law of Motion (constant mass, introductory)
format: Small introductory study brief (standalone); not a full textbook treatment.

contract.audience: Introductory physics learner (e.g. senior secondary level) meeting the stated prerequisites
learning_outcome: Define system, external force, net external force, mass, and acceleration.
State Newton’s second law in words and as F_net = m a for constant mass, including direction and proportional relationships.
Use a = F_net / m to calculate acceleration in a simple one-dimensional situation.
Explain, within scope, how changing net force or mass affects acceleration.

extent.topic: Newton’s second law for a chosen system with constant mass (introductory classical mechanics)
in_scope: External forces and net external force as the cause of acceleration
Qualitative meaning and basic quantitative use of F_net = m a
Simple one-dimensional situations or same-direction net force/acceleration
conditions: Classical (Newtonian) mechanics; everyday scales and speeds much less than c
prerequisites: Basic ideas of force, mass, velocity, and acceleration
Basic algebra and SI units (N, kg, m/s^2)
out_of_scope: Multi-force 2D/3D vector component resolution beyond net force and direction
Detailed force models and complex multi-body setups except simple external forces
Extended problem-solving strategies or large question banks
extent.completeness_claim: Complete for the stated learning outcome within the stated scope and conditions; limits explicitly stated.
